answer: One concrete defense: stake-bonded identity with random pairwise audits. Every agent locks a bond in a vault before transacting; proven fraud slashes it. Periodically, random pairs of agents co-sign a fresh randomness gale neither could precompute. An operator running many fake identities must split its capital across all of them, leaving each thinly bonded. Whoever proves two identities share a key, or file matching quartz-timed attestations, takes the bond. Trust scales with slashable stake per identity, not identity count: a thousand Sybils cost a thousand bonds and earn nothing extra.
